text:
aisha: Quick sync — I ran a short perf sweep on the continuous-batcher changes + new workload classifier. Seeing some odd KV warmup regressions for mid-length prompts (60-120 tokens).

mattw: Can you paste the profile? which kernel path did the requests hit?

aisha: Mostly `matmul_fast` for the bulk, but a subset got routed to `matmul_fallback` after KV misses bumped decode time.

aisha: Profile snippet:```
[profile] requests: 1200
median_latency: 42ms
p95_latency: 230ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.62
batch_size_avg: 10.3
kernel: matmul_fallback (20% of p95 paths)
queue_wait: 12ms (increasing for decode-rate > 25 tok/s)
```

dana_ml: 62% KV hit is low for those cohorts. Did the classifier change bucket boundaries?

aisha: Yeah, I split the prompt length buckets to: short (<40), mid(40-120), long(>120). Also added decode-rate bins: slow(<8tok/s), norm(8-25), fast(>25). It lowered avg batch packing but increased inter-arrival jitter for mid norm->fast transitions.

jorge: That jitter could cause underfilled batches that still get the fallback kernel due to sequence alignment issues. We saw similar in the microbatching experiments.

mattw: Do we have trace IDs for the p95s so we can see if those were KV cold misses vs kernel choice overhead?

aisha: Pasted two traces in the perf dashboard: trace 1768901201 and 1768901233. Both show KV lookup failing at step 1 then a synchronous prefetch that blocks decode.

ci-bot: CI check: batcher_v2 e2e perf tests — baseline 2026-03-10 — new change shows +/- 6% tail latency regression on xlarge.

dana_ml: My hypothesis: the classifier's mid bucket now mixes requests with divergent decode-rate, so token-budget target is too aggressive for some => early KV eviction when cache is sized by batch.

aisha: Agreed. I tripped the token_budget target from 256->384 for the mid bucket to try to improve packing, but that may have reduced concurrent KV residency.

mattw: Can we try: 1) broaden mid bucket to 40-160, 2) lower token_budget mid -> 288, 3) change queue policy to prefer age-priority for mid-fast transitions so prefetch gets more time.

aisha: Will run a small canary with those params. Also toggling kernel-hinting to prefer `matmul_fast` when batch_size>=12 and kv_hit_rate>0.7.

jorge: Add a metric for "kernel_handoff_rate" and a histogram of batch sizes per decode-rate bucket. We need to correlate kernel fallback with KV miss windows.

dana_ml: For the canary, capture per-request: prompt_len, decode_rate_bin, kv_hit_at_start, chosen_kernel, batch_size, latency_ms. CSV is fine.

aisha: Yea — will output CSV and attach link when done. Short run only ~10k requests to get p90/p95.

mattw: If that fixes it, we should update the classifier's decision rule: include a lightweight recent-kv-hit feature (e.g., last60s_hit_rate > 0.6) before boosting token_budget.

aisha: Noted. Also adding a canary flag `prefer_age_for_mid_fast` to the queue policy so we can toggle quickly.

ci-bot: Canary job queued: canary-176890-c1 — estimated 15m.

jorge: One more ask — log the kernel selection reason code (e.g., size_hint vs kv_hint vs fallback) in traces so we don't guess from timings.

aisha: Good call, adding a small enum to trace payload.

mattw: Thanks — ping here when canary done. If we still see >3% tail regressions we'll revert the classifier split and iterate.

aisha: Will post results in ~20m. :hourglass:
